ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Lorraine Hansberry — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: After six cycles: restaging CT and CA 19-9, decision for surgery, and preparation for pancreaticoduodenectomy

text.paragraph: Review after six cycles: restaging results and the decision for surgery. [S]

Ms. Hansberry returns two weeks after her sixth and last cycle before surgery. The diarrhea after cycle 5 settled within two days with loperamide, fluids and potassium, and with irinotecan reduced for cycle 6 she had only two loose stools. The restaging CT four days ago shows the tumor smaller and less contact with the vein, with no spread, and the tumor board recommends surgery; she met the surgeon and has chosen to go ahead. The interim CT ordered before cycle 5 was never scheduled. The cold-induced tingling is fading and her fingertips feel almost normal. Pain is 1 out of 10 and she takes oxycodone once every few days. She walks 30 minutes a day to prepare for surgery. Home fasting glucose is 115 to 135 mg/dL. She has had no bleeding on apixaban. She has written most mornings this month. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1963-08-10; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 54.2 kg; blood pressure 112/72, pulse 80
Soft, non-tender; no mass; port site clean
Light touch at the fingertips almost normal; vibration and reflexes normal
Calm, focused, asks about recovery time for writing

Epigastric pain for about two months, boring through to the back and worse after meals and lying flat, with nausea, early fullness, a loss of 5 kg (8 percent of her weight), and pale, loose stools: an upper abdominal cause such as a bleeding ulcer or a pancreatic or duodenal tumor must be found. Upper endoscopy and pancreas-protocol CT booked this week
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented collapse in pain and the account of a suspected duodenal ulcer. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic upper gastrointestinal blood loss: black stools on and off for three weeks, two near-fainting spells, hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, MCV 74 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL
S — Synthetic finding anchored to the documented account that she was told she had anemia and bleeding ulcers.

New hyperglycemia: A1c 6.6% and random glucose 132 mg/dL in a lean woman of 32 who is losing weight; new diabetes with weight loss can be the first sign of a pancreatic cancer, so it is to be confirmed and explained, not labeled type 2
S — Synthetic finding; superseded when diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer was recorded at the second visit.

Adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas, 3.1 cm, invading the duodenum, borderline resectable (tumor contact of more than half the circumference of the superior mesenteric vein, no arterial contact), no distant spread, CA 19-9 486 U/mL after biliary drainage; on EUS-guided biopsy; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented cancer, whose primary site the sources record differently
S — Synthetic histology, site, stage and course; the sources say she died of cancer and differ on whether it was pancreatic, duodenal, or colonic with spread to the pancreas (R). See sources.md.
Diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer (pancreatogenic, type 3c): A1c 6.6% at intake and fasting glucose 141 mg/dL
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor.
Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency from obstruction of the pancreatic duct: pale, floating, loose stools after fatty meals and weight loss
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor; diagnosed clinically, as guidance allows in pancreatic cancer.
Cancer-related pain in the upper abdomen and back, 6 out of 10, with sleep broken by it
S — Synthetic symptom of the synthetic tumor.
Obstruction of the distal common bile duct by the tumor, relieved by a covered metal stent placed at ERCP
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor.

Chemotherapy-induced diarrhea from irinotecan, grade 2 (five to six watery stools a day above her usual), starting on day 3 of cycle 5, with low potassium and magnesium and mild dehydration; no fever, blood or neutropenia; resolved
S — Synthetic treatment effect; not a historical claim.

Oxaliplatin peripheral neuropathy, grade 1: tingling in the fingers and toes in the cold, lasting a few days after each cycle, with mild tingling at the fingertips between cycles; no effect on writing or buttons
S — Synthetic common effect of oxaliplatin.

list.item:
Pancreatic head adenocarcinoma, borderline resectable, after six cycles of modified FOLFIRINOX (C25.0). A partial response on CT and CA 19-9 41 U/mL from 486, with no progression, so resection is recommended by the tumor board. Fit for surgery: albumin 3.6 g/dL, weight 2 percent below the weight at diagnosis, normal kidney and liver function, INR 1.0. [S]
Pylorus-preserving pancreaticoduodenectomy with superior mesenteric vein resection in two weeks.
Stop apixaban three days before surgery; enoxaparin for four weeks after it.
Continue walking and protein supplements until surgery.

Chemotherapy-induced diarrhea (K52.1). Resolved after the cycle 5 episode; only two loose stools after cycle 6 at the reduced irinotecan dose. [S]
Problem resolved.

Diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer (E08.9). A1c 7.0% and glucose 124 mg/dL on no treatment. Resection of the head of the pancreas often worsens diabetes; insulin may be needed after surgery. [S]
Glucose monitoring in hospital, with basal insulin if needed.

Oxaliplatin neuropathy, grade 1 (G62.0). Fading two weeks after the last oxaliplatin dose. [S]
Review after surgery.

Follow-up: Surgery in two weeks. Primary care review about six weeks after surgery with the pathology. Call for fever, bleeding, or leg swelling before then. Next scheduled visit 1963-10-05: six weeks after pancreaticoduodenectomy: pathology, diabetes and enzyme replacement after surgery, and the plan for chemotherapy after surgery. [S]
